To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lock contention probability is the dominant factor in determining the overall performance of a multi-system environment.
the performance of multi-systems is very sensitive to system parameters such as the number of systems, the number of users, the size of the data base and the degree of concurrency control.

the probability of lock contentions in the multi-system environment is a function of the number of users and of the number of systems, and that the data base buffer invalidations in a multi-system data base sharing environment are a function of the data base buffer size, the data base buffer replacement algorithm, the number of users, the system load, the number of systems and the lock contentions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a methodology and a framework for performance analysis of multiple systems sharing data, and for evaluating design alternatives.
the performance of a multi-system architecture with a common data base and centralized lock engine.
the development of a methodology to predict the performance of multi-systems sharing a common data-base in a multi-system, multi-processor environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a multi-system environment can be made to work, but that there are significant performance penalties associated with the sharing of the data base, especially in terms of response time, throughput and data base availability.
the multi-system environment can be expected to perform as well as a single large system, but that the performance of the multi-system environment is very sensitive to the workload characteristics.
a multi-system architecture can provide a significant improvement in performance over the single-system architecture for the workload and system parameters studied here.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a multi-system environment can achieve performance comparable to a single system environment if the number of concurrent users is limited and if the data base buffer invalidations are minimized.
the performance of multiple systems is affected by the number of systems, the workload characteristics and system parameters such as buffer size and lock granularity.

the use of a centralized lock engine for concurrency control in multi-system environments can result in a performance penalty, and that the use of multiple local lock engines is more effective in reducing the performance penalty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multi-system performance depends on many factors, and that a simple analysis of lock contention probability is not sufficient to predict the overall multi-system performance.

multi-system data sharing performance is sensitive to the system workload and to system parameters, and that a centralized concurrency control approach is not necessarily inferior to a distributed approach.
the multi-system environment is more sensitive to system parameters than a single system.
